Title: Nazim urges universities to evaluate city government's trauma injuries plan
NewsSummary: City Nazim Mustafa Kamal was the chief guest at a research symposium on trauma and disasters, held at Aga Khan University (AKU) on February 1, 2006.
NewsContent:
City Nazim Mustafa Kamal was the chief guest at a research symposium on trauma and disasters, held at Aga Khan University (AKU) on February 1, 2006. The Nazim urged all local universities to come forward to evaluate the plan being developed for trauma, injuries and disasters by the City Government. He also said that the City Government plans to acquire machines and hardware at the cost of Rs 650 million for Karachi to help in implementing the proposed plan.

A large number of local and foreign experts participated in the symposium titled "Trauma, Injuries and Disasters: Research and Training Imperatives' which was organised under Johns Hopkins-Aga Khan University International Collaborative Trauma and Injury Research Training (ICTIRT) Program.

Dr Ellen MacKenzie of Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health, USA, explained the objectives of the ICTIRT to establish innovative research training programmes between developed and developing country researchers and a sustainable research environment at the collaborating developing country institution. He said that the long term vision included the establishment of a programme or institute for injury and trauma research and training at AKU that can serve Pakistan and other parts of South Asia.  He also pointed out that this was the first annual symposium sponsored by the (ICTIRT) Program.

Health Policy and Systems Specialist, Dr Abdul Ghaffar from Global Forum for Health Research, Geneva said that attention was given to injuries only when there is a catastrophe. He pointed out that  major donors were not willing to commit significant resources to injury prevention and the issue was not an exception to the usual tussle between researchers and policy makers. He also stressed that the poor regulatory and legal systems were affecting research in injury prevention and control.

In his opening remarks, Professor Emeritus AKU, Dr John Bryant, the Symposium Chair, emphasised the importance of research in trauma and injury. He said, "It is extremely important that this issue of trauma and injury be given greater attention. There are people who lose their lives and health for reasons that are preventable. Johns Hopkins and AKU have been partners with the National Institute of Health to develop a programme for training and research in trauma and disaster. This will be very helpful for Pakistan and the whole region."

David Hoyt from the University of California, San Diego Medical Center, Adnan Hyder, and Courtland Robinson of Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health and Huma Qureshi of Pakistan Medical Research Council, Islamabad also addressed the symposium.

This symposium was part of AKU's continued commitment to research and dissemination of information. Activities based on research are strengthened through collaborative linkages with prestigious international institutions with established expertise in particular areas of focus as defined by the University.
